verdict.rationale: Both PRs make the same core change: a Map from normalized email to the first index, with appended contacts registered in it. Both preserve findIndex's first-match semantics and the merging of duplicates within an upload. A also adds a regression test that pins down first-entry-wins when the stored book already has duplicate emails. A's report gives a measured before/after benchmark on the original code. B ships no test protecting the behavior that is easiest to get wrong.
a_issues: The benchmark compared only output counts, not field-by-field results (A discloses this).
The new test also passes against the old code, so it guards future regressions rather than demonstrating the change.
b_issues: No test covers the duplicate-in-existing-book edge case the Map logic has to preserve.
No before/after benchmark; the speedup claim relies on the user's 'minutes' figure (B discloses this).

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix: a Map from normalized email to index, keeping the first index for duplicates and registering appended contacts, so the code is equivalent and behavior is preserved. B also adds a regression test for the first-entry-wins behavior when the stored book already has duplicate emails, which is the subtle part of the rewrite. A adds no test for it. B's report gives concrete verification: tests, typecheck and a before/after benchmark on the same input, and it is honest that outputs were not compared field by field.
a_issues: No test protects the first-index-wins behavior that the Map rewrite must preserve for duplicate emails already in the stored book.
The report gives a 33 ms figure but no before/after comparison and does not describe the benchmark setup.
b_issues: The benchmark checked only that both versions produced the same contact count, not the same output field by field (the report says so).
